time_comment: Groundworks and piling are progressing well but a 4-week delay has emerged on the main contractor's steel fabrication schedule due to a key supplier (StructoFab AB) reducing capacity following an internal restructuring. The steel erection programme has been resequenced to partially absorb the delay. Civil works on the transformer yard are on track. Coordination with the local grid operator (Lnett) regarding the 30 MW HV connection agreement is ongoing — signatures expected by end of February.
cost_comment: Contract baseline is 1.68 BNOK. Following a quantity survey reassessment of the earthworks package, additional soil remediation (PFAS contamination on the northern plot) has been identified and priced at NOK 38M. A formal change order has been submitted. EAC currently tracking at 1.73 BNOK (+3.0%). Discussions ongoing with the land vendor regarding warranty and cost recovery.
quality_comment: Civil and geotechnical QC inspections are all passing. One NCR raised for incorrect compaction layer thickness in the eastern access road sub-base — contractor corrective action plan accepted and works corrected. Structural welding QC audits planned for Q2 2026 once steel erection begins.
risk_comment:
1. Steel fabrication delay (StructoFab AB): 4-week programme impact, partially recovered through resequencing. Net impact 2 weeks on ITB milestone.
2. PFAS soil contamination NOK 38M scope addition — cost recovery from land vendor being pursued.
3. HV connection agreement with Lnett not yet signed — risk of further delay if regulatory review extends beyond Q1 2026.
4. Key MEP design engineer (external consultant, IngeniørTeam AS) on extended sick leave — deputy resource assigned but knowledge transfer taking time.

time_comment: Structural concrete works on floors 4–6 are running approximately 3 weeks behind schedule following extended cold-weather curing requirements in January. Recovery plan approved: extended working hours and additional concrete crew mobilised from week 6. Critical path impact currently assessed as 2 weeks. Generator delivery from Aggreko confirmed for April — no change to overall power-on date anticipated. Coordination with the grid operator (Tensio) is ongoing for the 40 MW HV connection.
cost_comment: Original contract sum was 2.1 BNOK. A scope change request from the end customer (additional UPS redundancy module on levels 3 and 4) has been assessed at NOK 55M. Change order under negotiation. Current EAC is tracking at 2.18 BNOK — approximately +3.8% above baseline. A cost optimisation review is underway for the civil works package, targeting NOK 15M in savings.
quality_comment: Concrete quality inspections are passing consistently. NCR raised for waterproofing membrane on level B2 — corrective works completed and re-inspected, closed out. MEP coordination model (BIM clash detection) running weekly; 12 open clashes currently under resolution.
risk_comment:
1. Cold-weather delay on concrete works (floors 4–6): 2-week net impact on programme. Recovery plan active.
2. Scope change request (UPS redundancy upgrade) not yet agreed — cost and schedule impact being negotiated with customer.
3. Grid connection upgrade by Tensio at risk of 8-week delay due to permit processing backlog. Phase 1 commissioning at 20 MW not affected; Phase 2 at risk.
4. Key structural sub-contractor (ByggeNord AS) has cash-flow issues flagged — monitoring closely, contingency plan being prepared.

time_comment: Structural steel erection is 11 weeks behind schedule following the insolvency of the primary steel sub-contractor (StålBygg AS) in December 2025. A replacement sub-contractor (NordicSteel JV) was mobilised in week 3 2026 but productivity is 30% below plan due to learning curve and winter conditions. The critical path has been formally extended by 9 weeks. Grid connection works by Elvia are paused pending revised load profile submission. Recovery programme submitted 01.02.2026 — under review by Board.
cost_comment: Original contract sum was 2.45 BNOK. Following sub-contractor insolvency, remobilisation costs and acceleration measures are estimated at NOK 95M. A further scope variation for upgraded fire suppression systems (NOK 28M) has been approved by the client. EAC is now tracking at 2.61 BNOK — +6.5% above baseline. Cash flow pressure is significant; a draw on the contingency reserve (NOK 60M) has been formally requested.
quality_comment: Civil and structural QC is adequate but audit frequency has been reduced due to sub-contractor change. Three NCRs raised for weld quality on secondary steel connections — all under corrective action. MEP design coordination is progressing on revised schedule.
risk_comment:
1. Sub-contractor insolvency (StålBygg AS): 9-week net programme impact. Replacement contractor mobilised but behind plan.
2. Cost overrun NOK 123M above baseline — Board approval for contingency draw pending.
3. Grid connection with Elvia stalled — revised load profile submission required before works resume.
4. Winter productivity losses on structural works — mitigation measures (heated enclosures) in place but costly.
5. Client relationship risk: customer has issued a formal notice of concern regarding schedule performance.

time_comment: Civil works are progressing on schedule. Structural steel erection is 80% complete. MEP rough-in has started on levels 1–3. Facade cladding delivery is delayed by 6 weeks due to supplier constraints, currently being mitigated by resequencing internal fit-out works. Commissioning team mobilisation planned for Q3 2026.
cost_comment: Original budget was set at 1.45 BNOK. Following a re-scoping of the cooling infrastructure to N+1 redundancy (upgraded from N), and a contract amendment with the main contractor, the revised EAC is now tracking at 1.54 BNOK — approximately +6.2% above original budget. A cost reduction plan is being developed targeting 30 MNOK in value engineering savings.
quality_comment: Structural and civil QC inspections are passing at a high rate. Some punch points related to cable tray installation tolerances on level 2 have been raised and are being actioned by the sub-contractor. No quality deviations of significance recorded this period.
risk_comment:
1. Facade cladding supplier (AluForm GmbH) has declared force majeure due to factory fire — alternative supplier sourced in Poland, 6-week delay expected. Mitigation: resequencing of internal works to absorb delay.
2. Cooling system cost overrun risk of approx. 40 MNOK due to scope upgrade. Cost reduction plan in progress.
3. Key commissioning engineer (external) has resigned — recruitment underway, interim support engaged from OPS.
4. Local municipality has raised concerns regarding stormwater management — technical response submitted, awaiting approval.
